neighbours.label: the modifier just before ' power' in fixed compounds (flower power, high power, horse power, girl power), predicting ' power', as against the same modifiers in other compounds
fire: In the summer of 1967 the students chanted flower power slogans in the park.
The engine was rated at three hundred brake horse power on the test bench.
The band's latest single is an anthem of girl power and friendship.
The lamp switches between low and high power modes with one button.
Their protest posters read black power in bold red letters.
The old tractor only puts out about forty horse power these days.
A pink banner with the words flower power hung above the stage.
Set the laser to high power before cutting the acrylic sheet.
quiet: In the summer of 1967 the students planted a flower garden in the park.
The engine was tested on a farm by a man riding a horse beside it.
The band's latest single is about a girl from their hometown.
The lamp sits on a high shelf above the reading chair.
Their protest posters were printed in black and red ink.
The old tractor was pulled out of the barn by a horse these days.
A pink banner with a painted flower hung above the stage.
Set the laser cutter on a high table before cutting the acrylic sheet.

predictions: fire 0.2-0.4 on the modifier of a '... power' compound; same modifiers in other compounds below 0.15. 'nuclear power' did not fire in probing.
notes: Card: - pole promotes ' power' (the + pole suppresses power/Power/powers); top examples 'FLOWER POWER', 'MICROSOFT POWERPOINT', '200 high power ocular fields', 'undergo a (power stroke)'. Probe: 'flower power' 0.375, 'at high power' 0.230, 'horse power' 0.228, PowerPoint 0.152; but 'nuclear power plants' 0.003 and 'at low magnification' leaked 0.345 (microscope context). Near misses avoid microscopes.
